etymology: Webster 1828 treats DONE as the participle passive of do (Dun. See Do): performed; executed; finished. He then records the wager-sense: a word by which agreement to a proposal is expressed (done = it is agreed). This page fills the KJV-gap participle. Companion pages already treat work, deeds, and command.
biblical_def: Done in Scripture is not a shrug and not a wager. It names the will of God brought to pass, the deed already committed, and the counsel that will not be rewritten. The Lord’s Prayer does not ask heaven to copy earth: Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven (Matt 6:10). Gethsemane does not negotiate a second will: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done (Luke 22:42). Eden will not let the woman call the Fall a misunderstanding: What is this that thou hast done? (Gen 3:13). The throne will not leave history open-ended: It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end (Rev 21:6). Isaiah will not let tomorrow ambush the decree: the things that are not yet done are already declared, and My counsel shall stand (Isa 46:10). The dictionary therefore keeps done from becoming either fatalism or unfinished business. It is the Bible’s way of saying: performed, finished, and settled as the Lord has willed.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines DONE as the participle of do: performed; executed; finished; and as the word of agreement to a proposal (as in a wager: done, that is, it is agreed).
webster_full: DONE, participle passive Dun. See Do.
1. Performed; executed; finished.
2. A word by which agreement to a proposal is expressed; as in laying a wager, an offer being made, the person accepting or agreeing says, done; that is, it is agreed, I agree, I accept.
scriptures: Matthew 6:10
Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
Luke 22:42
Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.
Genesis 3:13
And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.
Revelation 21:6
And he said unto me, It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely.
Isaiah 46:10
Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure:
corruption_summary: Done is corrupted when Thy will be done is treated as a mood, when What hast thou done? is treated as a closed case with no repentance, and when It is done is denied so that God’s counsel can still be edited.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to steal Matthew 6:10 as atmosphere. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven is petition under a King, not a mindfulness slogan. Therapeutic religion keeps the cadence and drops the King. The recovery is Gethsemane: not my will, but thine, be done (Luke 22:42).

The second corruption is cheap closure on Genesis 3:13. What is this that thou hast done? is indictment, not a shrug that “what’s done is done.” Antinomian talk treats finished sin as finished business. The woman’s deed is named; the serpent’s lie is named; the need is atonement, not rebranding.

The third corruption is to keep history unwritten against Revelation 21:6 and Isaiah 46:10. Open theism and process theology will not let the Alpha and Omega say It is done, and they will not let counsel stand before the thing is done. The participle remains the Lord’s. The creature does not get a rewrite.
roots_summary: Webster: performed; executed; finished. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek ginomai (G1096) at Matthew 6:10, Luke 22:42, and Revelation 21:6; Hebrew asah (H6213) at Isaiah 46:10. Genesis 3:13 carries no Strong’s tag on done in this cache; this page does not mint one.
roots_lines: Greek ginomai (G1096) — to come to be, to be brought to pass (Matt 6:10; Luke 22:42; Rev 21:6, It is done).
Hebrew asah (H6213) — to do, to make, to accomplish (Isa 46:10, the things that are not yet done).
Genesis 3:13 is KJV-verified; the cache does not tag done with a Hebrew number on that verse line. No lemma is invented here.
Philippians 2:3 English done has no Strong’s tag on the participle in this cache; that line is not treated as a minted done-lemma on this page.
usage: Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven (Matt 6:10) — petition, not a mood.
Gethsemane: not my will, but thine, be done (Luke 22:42).
The Fall is a deed named (What is this that thou hast done?, Gen 3:13); the throne answers with It is done (Rev 21:6), and counsel stands before the thing is done (Isa 46:10).

etymology: Webster 1828 treats MANY as adjective (numerous; comprising a great number of individuals) and as noun (a multitude; a great number of individuals; the people; formerly also a retinue). His own biblical illustrations include Genesis 17:4 (a father of many nations), 1 Corinthians 1:26 (not many wise… not many mighty, not many noble), and the line Many are the afflictions of the righteous. This page fills the KJV-gap word of number. Companion pages already treat multitude, nations, and elect.
biblical_def: Many in Scripture is not a poll and not a proof. It names a real number under God’s hand — sometimes of mercy, often of ruin, never of a majority that outvotes the Lord. Paul will not let the church measure calling by pedigree: not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called (1 Cor 1:26). David will not let affliction be rare: Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all (Psa 34:19). Jesus will not let the crowd be the gate: wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat (Matt 7:13). He will not let invitation be confused with election: For many are called, but few are chosen (Matt 22:14). Paul will not let Adam and Christ be two private stories: by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous (Rom 5:19). The dictionary therefore keeps many from becoming either democracy-as-truth or a head-count gospel. It is the Bible’s way of saying: numerous — and still under the Lord’s decree.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines MANY as numerous (a great number of individuals) and as a noun, a multitude / the people. He illustrates from Genesis 17:4 and 1 Corinthians 1:26, and from the afflictions of the righteous.
webster_full: MANY, adjective men'ny.
1. Numerous; comprising a great number of individuals.
Thou shalt be a father of many nations. Genesis 17:4.
Not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called. 1 Corinthians 1:26.
MANY are the afflictions of the righteous.
It is often preceded by as or so, and followed by so, indicating an equal number.
It precedes an or a, before a noun in the singular number.
2. In low language, preceded by too, it denotes powerful or much; as, they are too many for us.
MANY, noun men'ny. A multitude; a great number of individuals; the people.
MANY, noun men'ny. A retinue of servants; household.
scriptures: 1 Corinthians 1:26
For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called:
Psalm 34:19
Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all.
Matthew 7:13
Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:
Matthew 22:14
For many are called, but few are chosen.
Romans 5:19
For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.
corruption_summary: Many is corrupted when the crowd is treated as the gate, when calling is measured by the noble, and when federal many in Adam and in Christ is flattened into a head-count that denies election.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is Matthew 7:13 inverted. Many there be which go in thereat is warning, not a missions metric. Attractional religion treats the broad way as success. The strait gate is still the gate. Majority is not mercy.

The second corruption is 1 Corinthians 1:26 with the labels swapped. Paul says not many wise… not many mighty, not many noble. Celebrity Christianity and prosperity talk hunt the noble and call it fruit. The recovery is the calling of God, not the resume of the flesh.

The third corruption is to steal Romans 5:19 for universalism, or to empty it into a private self-help. Many were made sinners… many be made righteous is Adam and Christ, federal and particular. It is not “everybody, therefore nobody in particular.” The many in Christ are the many He actually makes righteous.
roots_summary: Webster: numerous / a multitude. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek polus (G4183) at 1 Corinthians 1:26, Matthew 7:13, Matthew 22:14, and Romans 5:19; Hebrew rab (H7227) at Psalm 34:19. Genesis 17:4 carries no Strong’s tag on many in this cache; this page does not mint one.
roots_lines: Greek polus (G4183) — many, much (1 Cor 1:26; Matt 7:13; Matt 22:14; Rom 5:19).
Hebrew rab (H7227) — many, much, abundant (Psa 34:19, Many are the afflictions).
Genesis 17:4 is KJV-verified; the cache does not tag many with a Hebrew number on that verse line. No lemma is invented here.
Matthew 24:5 English many is G4183 in this cache on both occurrences; that verse is not needed as a fifth quotation on this page.
usage: Not many wise… not many mighty, not many noble, are called (1 Cor 1:26) — calling is not pedigree.
The righteous have many afflictions, and the LORD delivers out of them all (Psa 34:19).
Many take the broad way (Matt 7:13); many are called and few chosen (Matt 22:14); many are made sinners in Adam and righteous in Christ (Rom 5:19).

etymology: Webster 1828 treats HIMSELF as pronoun in the nominative or objective case (him and self): emphatic personality; discrimination of person when added to he or to a noun; the ordinary reciprocal; and, when a man has “come to himself,” his proper character after wandering. His own biblical illustrations include Judges 3:19, God himself as captain, and David hiding himself. This page fills the KJV-gap reflexive. Companion pages already treat humble, servant, and cross.
biblical_def: Himself in Scripture is not a brand and not a mirror. It names the Person who acts, and it will not let the creature steal the center. The Son did not empty a costume: he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross (Phil 2:8). He did not outsource the ransom: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity (Titus 2:14). He did not leave the purge to another priest: when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high (Heb 1:3). The Jews heard the claim and hated it: making himself equal with God (John 5:18). Husbands are not licensed to keep a private self: Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it (Eph 5:25). The dictionary therefore keeps himself from becoming either self-esteem or a kenosis that ungods the Son. It is the Bible’s way of saying: this Person, and no substitute.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines HIMSELF as the emphatic or reciprocal pronoun (him and self): he, with distinct personality; added to he or a noun for emphasis; the ordinary reciprocal (David hid himself); and a man come to himself after wandering.
webster_full: HIMSELF', pronoun In the nominative or objective case. him and self.
1. He; but himself is more emphatical, or more expressive of distinct personality than he.
2. When himself is added to he, or to a noun, it expresses discrimination of person with particular emphasis.
But he himself returned from the quarries. Judges 3:19.
But God himself is with us for our captain.
3. When used as the reciprocal pronoun, it is not usually emphatical.
David hid himself in the field. 1 Samuel 20:24.
4. It was formerly used as a substitute for neuter nouns; as high as heaven himself. This use is now improper.
5. himself is used to express the proper character, or natural temper and disposition of a person, after wandering of mind or irregularity. We say, a man has come to himself.
By himself, alone; unaccompanied.
scriptures: Philippians 2:8
And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.
Titus 2:14
Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.
Hebrews 1:3

Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
John 5:18
Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.
Ephesians 5:25
Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;
corruption_summary: Himself is corrupted when the Son’s himself is emptied of deity, when the cross is recast as self-care, and when the church is loved as a brand instead of a people He gave himself for.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is kenosis as un-godding. Philippians 2:8 is he humbled himself unto the death of the cross; John 5:18 is making himself equal with God. The one Person is not a man who later became useful. He is the brightness of glory who by himself purged sins (Heb 1:3). Process Christology and every reduced Jesus keep the pronoun and drop the Person.

The second corruption is the self-esteem gospel. Therapeutic religion hears himself as the project: find yourself, forgive yourself, love yourself first. Titus 2:14 is the opposite: He gave himself for us to redeem us from iniquity, not to baptize the old man. The recovery is crucifixion of the flesh, not a better mirror.

The third corruption is Ephesians 5:25 as marketing. Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it is particular love unto blood. Attractional talk loves a crowd and keeps the self. Husbands are commanded the same shape: give yourself, do not keep a private throne.
roots_summary: Webster: emphatic / reciprocal pronoun (him and self). Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek heautou (G1438) at Philippians 2:8, Titus 2:14, Hebrews 1:3, John 5:18, and Ephesians 5:25. Judges 3:19, 2 Chronicles 13:12, and 1 Samuel 20:24 carry no Strong’s tag on himself in this cache; this page does not mint Hebrew numbers for those lines.
roots_lines: Greek heautou (G1438) — of himself, himself (Phil 2:8; Titus 2:14; Heb 1:3; John 5:18; Eph 5:25).
John 5:18 also tags equal as G2470 on that verse line; the equality claim is not treated as a minted himself-lemma.
Judges 3:19, 2 Chronicles 13:12, and 1 Samuel 20:24 are KJV-verified Webster illustrations; the cache does not tag himself with a Hebrew number on those verse lines. No lemma is invented here.
Philippians 2:7 English himself is likewise G1438 in this cache (made himself of no reputation); that line is companion to 2:8, not a second invented root.
usage: He humbled himself… even the death of the cross (Phil 2:8) — the Person acts; He is not emptied of deity.
He gave himself for us to redeem and to purify a people unto himself (Titus 2:14); He gave himself for the church (Eph 5:25).
By himself He purged sins (Heb 1:3); making himself equal with God was the claim the Jews heard (John 5:18).
